meta.title: The D Form: Small, High, and Always a Fragment
meta.summary: The D form's octave jump is +3 frets instead of +2 because it crosses the B string, and its upper root sits one fret past the twelfth-fret marker.

It's the same irregularity the C form flagged first: its higher-sounding root sat two frets nearer the nut than expected, and the B string was named as the cause without the arithmetic behind it. Here is that arithmetic, and it closes the loop — every odd lean in this chapter's roots traces back to the one string that isn't tuned a fourth from its neighbour.

of the five, and essentially never played whole. The full D-form barre isn't a thing players do — it lives as a top-strings fragment from the start, not as a whole shape someone gave up on. That fragment is genuinely useful rather than a consolation prize: it's the highest place this chord lives before the neck repeats itself, and it sits exactly where a lead line is probably already sitting, so grabbing two or three notes of it costs no repositioning at all. Reuse the fragment habit from the C form; this is the same idea in its tightest spot.
Don't try to hold the full D-form barre. It isn't a stretch worth fighting for — take the top-strings fragment instead.
Every window in this chapter is the same five frets wide — the D form isn't smaller because its window is narrower, it's smaller because only two of the six
s in the first twelve frets happen to fall inside it. Where the G and E forms each caught three, this one catches two.
Look at that upper root again:
sits one fret past the twelfth-fret marker, and it is the same note as
— the C form's upper root — an octave higher. Fret 12 is where the nut's own pattern comes back around, so right after the D form the ladder starts again with the C form, up at fret 12.
Stop here and take stock: five forms, five windows, every root of
in the first twelve frets accounted for. Nothing about finding a root anywhere on this neck should require counting from open string any more.
That wrap-around, and what it means for the whole neck at once, is where the chapter closes next.
